back: To talk about work when you are not at work, especially with colleagues in a social setting.
Describes a job with standard daytime hours, typically in an office.
To record the time you arrive at work, often using an electronic card or clock.
A system where employees can choose their start and finish times within certain limits.
Trapped in a boring, repetitive job or situation that is difficult to change.
Having a very large amount of work to complete.
Working for several different organizations rather than being employed by one specific company.
A job that involves physical work rather than mental or office work.
A job that requires specific skills and training, often regarded as a calling (e.g., nursing or teaching).
An arrangement where two people share the hours, duties, and pay of one full-time position.
